A `GeometryPlan` holds everything about your layout that every solver shares:
the drawn component, its layer stack and materials, the Nets you declare, the
vacuum region, the Surface-EPR films and the lumped elements. `plan.prepare()` freezes it into a
*snapshot*, and each simulation takes that snapshot with `set_plan`. SCGSim's
geometry builder, SGB, then builds the 3D model from it, the same model for
Palace and AEDT. This page gives the calls in order, what each one checks,
how to declare the lumped elements, which curves a plan accepts, and how to
cut a 2D cross-section. [Prepare a layout](../../guides/prepare-a-layout.qmd) walks
through a real plan; how the plan works inside is on
[GeometryPlan internals](../../contribute/internals/geometry-plan.qmd).

## Build a plan {#component-to-backend-geometry-contract}

These are the plan calls of the [First simulation](../../start/first-simulation.qmd),
a 200 µm pad in a 1000 µm die:

```python
plan = GeometryPlan(
    component=component,
    root_id="chip",
    layer_stack=get_single_die_layer_stack(),
    material_records=get_material_records(),
    coupon_padding_um=0.0,
)
plan.set_nets({"pad": ("chip/PAD",), "ground": ("chip/GROUND",)})
plan.set_vacuum_region(padding=(0.0, 0.0, 1000.0))
sim.set_plan(plan.prepare())
```

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| `GeometryPlan(component=..., root_id=..., layer_stack=..., material_records=..., coupon_padding_um=...)` | Takes the assembled GDSFactory component, the PDK layer stack and materials. `root_id` names the root occurrence; every Entity ID starts with it (`chip/PAD`). |
| `register_instance("chip/q0", reference)` | Names a child component placed in the layout, so its Entities become `chip/q0/...`. Register parents before children, one call per GDS reference; expand an array reference into single references first. `prepare()` refuses a child with its own component semantics that is not registered (`ValueError`, "it is not registered"): flattening the layout would otherwise lose its semantics. |
| `plan.entities` | The Entities of the plan, each with its qualified `.semantic_id`. |
| `set_nets({net_id: (entity_id, ...)})` | Declares which Entities form each Net: one piece of metal that is one conductor. SCGSim never infers a Net from shapes that touch. An Entity belongs to at most one Net; an Entity in no Net stays unassigned. An update with an unknown Entity, or one in two Nets, is refused whole. |
| `set_vacuum_region(padding=...)` | The box of empty space around the model, in µm: one number, an (x, y, z) tuple, or one value per face. |
| `set_surface_epr(specs)` | The Surface-EPR films and their inset margins, by interface type; see the [Eigenmode reference](palace-eigenmode.qmd#surface-epr-margins). |
| `set_lumped_elements(elements)` | The device's lumped elements, each on a port sheet the layout draws: a junction or an R, L, C element, or an excitation port; see [below](#lumped-elements). |
| `set_entity_priorities({entity_id: priority})` | Decides which of two overlapping Entities of one Net owns the overlap; see [below](#overlap-priority). |
| `prepare()` | Checks the declarations and returns the snapshot: the normalized geometry, the stack, the GDS bytes and the occurrence records, with no live reference to the component. |

The checks at `prepare()` and their errors are listed under
[What a layout must guarantee](../supported-scope.qmd#layout-rules). To change
anything, change the plan, prepare a new snapshot and call `set_plan` again.

### The grid {#the-grid}

The model grid is the layout's database unit, read from the GDS: 1 nm for an
OrcaPen SC PDK layout. Set it before you draw the cells. Every XY coordinate of
the model lies on that grid; heights, film thicknesses and the mesh do not.
SCGSim does not change the PDK's or GDSFactory's settings.

### Which region owns an overlap {#overlap-priority}

Overlapping regions are resolved in this order:

1. **Conductors before everything else.** Metal is placed first; solution
   regions never compete with it.
2. **A dielectric over vacuum**, whatever their `mesh_order`.
3. **Between two dielectrics, the lower `LayerLevel.mesh_order` wins**, the
   GDSFactory convention.
4. **Between two Entities of one Net, the higher priority wins**: the
   component's annotation `priority`, or `plan.set_entity_priorities(...)` for
   occurrences placed over each other. Equal or missing priorities are an
   `OverlapError` that names both Entities. Two conductors of different Nets
   may not overlap at all.

For example, a 20 × 20 µm silicon nitride patch with `mesh_order=1` on a
silicon region with `mesh_order=2`: the overlap is silicon nitride. Had the
patch been vacuum, the silicon would own the overlap, whatever the numbers.
Internally the plan stores `priority = -mesh_order`, so a stored `priority`
always means the higher value wins.

### The vacuum region {#vacuum-region}

The vacuum region is the plan's. Set it before `prepare()` with
`plan.set_vacuum_region(padding=...)`, or use the stack's own `VACUUM_REGION`;
no padding is ever assumed. Palace and AEDT receive the same box, and a
simulation has no vacuum setting of its own. Where the vacuum has no planar
padding, the model ends at the layout's planar extent, which matters for a
conductor that touches that edge; see
[A conductor that touches the boundary at one point](../known-geometry-problems.qmd#boundary-point-pinch).
An authored gap volume between two dies, `D0_TO_D1_GAP`, stays a vacuum Entity
of its own inside the box.

On the outer faces of the vacuum, Palace leaves its natural boundary (PMC),
and HFSS assigns the same condition, Perfect H, to its Region.

### Ground metal from a child component {#ground-plane-contributions-user}

A child component can add metal to a ground plane of the root, such as the arm
of an Xmon's ground that reaches into its clearance. It declares
`component_semantics.ground_plane_contributions`: each record gives exactly
`local_id`, `plane_id` (the root plane it joins), `level` (the conductor level,
which must match that plane's), `layer` and `selector_point_um`. The metal
becomes part of that plane; it is not an Entity of its own and has no Net
entry. How the records are resolved is in
[the internals](../../contribute/internals/geometry-plan.qmd#ground-plane-contributions).

### Lumped elements {#lumped-elements}

[]{#explicit-rectangular-junctions}A lumped element is a part of the device
that the model does not draw as metal: a Josephson junction as its inductance,
a resistor, a capacitor, or the port a measurement drives. Each one sits on a
port sheet the component draws and declares among the ports of its
`component_semantics`, joining the two conductors the sheet lands on. Declare
every lumped element once, on the plan, by the qualified name of its sheet;
every simulation reads them from the snapshot:

```python
from scgsim.geometry import LumpedElement, LumpedPort

plan.set_lumped_elements([
    LumpedElement("chip/o_junction_lumped", inductance_h=10e-9),
    LumpedPort("chip/o_launcher", reference_net="ground", impedance_ohm=50.0),
])
```

| Record | What it is |
|---|---|
| `LumpedElement(sheet, *, resistance_ohm=None, inductance_h=None, capacitance_f=None)` | A resistance, an inductance and a capacitance in parallel, in ohm, henry and farad; give at least one. A junction is an element with an inductance and, if you model it, a capacitance. |
| `LumpedPort(sheet, *, reference_net, impedance_ohm)` | An excitation port: the conductor in `reference_net` is its reference, the other its signal, and `impedance_ohm` is its reference impedance. |

The ports are numbered first, in the order you give them: port 1 is the first
`LumpedPort`, row and column 1 of an S-matrix. The other elements follow in
their order, so in a study without ports the first element is Palace's port
`P1`. `prepare()` refuses, naming the element, its sheet's layer and its box
in µm: a name the layout does not draw; a sheet that lands on other than two
conductors; two conductors of one Net; a port whose `reference_net` is
neither conductor's Net. `snapshot.lumped_elements` holds the result, one
`LumpedElementRecord` each, with the sheet, its two conductors in the order of
the sheet's direction (`start`, `end`) and their Nets.

What each simulation does with each element is on
[Supported calculations](../supported-calculations.qmd#lumped-elements);
in short, Palace Eigenmode and HFSS Eigenmode realize every element and treat
a port as a load of its impedance, Palace Electrostatic and Q3D leave them
open, Palace Driven drives each port in turn and realizes the other elements
as loads, and HFSS Driven Terminal takes the two ports. Every realized element's
sheet is cut to the rectangle between its two conductors, the same in Palace
and AEDT. A sheet the plan declares nothing on is not part of a Palace or HFSS
model. For a normalized `GeometryBuildInput` built below the plan,
`with_rectangular_junctions(build_input, specs)` binds a sheet to its two
terminals with `RectangularJunctionSpec` and `JunctionTerminalBinding`.

## Source curves {#source-curves}

A layout reaches SGB as polygons, and you may declare curves on top of them.
SGB builds **line segments and circular arcs** exactly; it refuses spline
curves with `UnsupportedCurveError`. A curve drawn as a polygon is always
accepted ([Curved outlines drawn as polygons](../supported-geometry.qmd#curve-rule)).
Palace meshes the arcs on either route, and AEDT imports them as exact arcs in
the model's STEP.

`SourceCurveSpec` describes a curve in XY micrometres. Its kinds are
`line_segment` (two end points) and `circular_arc` (start, a point on the arc,
end); `interpolation_spline` and `bspline` can be declared but SGB refuses
them. An optional `parameter_interval` trims the curve without refitting it.

`BoundaryCurveChainSpec` binds an ordered closed boundary to `entity_id`,
`boundary_id` and `selector_point_um`. The selector point lies in the metal of
the Entity. `role="outer"` selects the outline; `role="hole", hole_index=0`
selects the first hole of that polygon, and its selector point still lies in
the metal, not in the hole.

A component declares `boundary_curves` or `boundary_reconstruction` records
with its local IDs; the plan qualifies them with the occurrence and applies
its transform once. For an assembled input, call
`plan.set_boundary_curves(records)` or `plan.set_boundary_reconstruction(records)`
with qualified IDs.

`GdsBoundaryReconstructionSpec` turns drawn polygon edges back into a circular
arc. It names the edges by `segment_indices`: index `i` is the edge from drawn
vertex `i` to vertex `(i + 1) % N`, in the order the GDS stores the polygon
(read it from the component, for example with `component.get_polygons()`,
because GDSFactory normalizes polygons as KLayout stores them). A closed circle
takes three `anchor_indices`; an open arc takes start, on-arc and end anchors.
Three anchors on one line define no circle and are refused at `prepare()`.
`closed=True` selects a whole ring. Two reconstructions may not claim the same
edges, and a ring made by fusing two drawn polygons has no drawn order, so a
reconstruction on it is refused.

## Routes {#current-surface-epr-direction}

A route is how the metal films become solver geometry.

| Route | What it models | Taken by |
|---|---|---|
| Route A | Each film is a zero-thickness perfect-conductor sheet; bumps stay finite shells | Palace (`set_route("A")`); AEDT `modeling="thin_film"` |
| Route B | Each conductor is a finite metal volume whose surface is a perfect conductor and whose inside is left out of the mesh | Palace (`set_route("B")`, the default) |
| Route C | Each conductor volume stays in the model | AEDT `modeling="solid"` |

Palace's `set_route` and `mesh()` refuse any route other than A and B with
`ValueError`. [Route A and Route B](../../concepts/routes.qmd) explains the
choice with a cross-section, and
[AEDT: solid or thin_film](aedt-runtime.qmd#aedt-solid-thin-film) gives the
heights under each. Surface-EPR bands are cut into the model on every route
when it is built.

## Films and profiles {#physical-representation}

How each film is turned into a sheet or a volume, and how the heights of the
stack change, is set by an approximation profile.
[Physical representation](physical-representation.qmd) lists the profiles and
the Palace calls that choose them.

## 2D cross-sections {#section-models}

SGB can cut the 3D model along a line to give the 2D model of a long, uniform
line, such as a CPW. The 2D model has the 3D model's Entities, Nets,
materials and Surface-EPR bands by construction. No solver of this version
reads it; [Q2D](aedt-runtime.qmd#q2d-native-combined-matrix-export) takes a
cross-section you describe instead.

For example, `finite_ground_cpw_coupon` at the OrcaPen SC PDK defaults (signal
10 µm, gaps 6 µm, grounds 80 µm, Al 100 nm on 500 µm Si), Route B with MA, MS
and SA bands at margins 0.5 and 1.0 µm and the vacuum padded by (0, 0, 1000) µm,
cut across its middle at x = 0, gives this section:

| Region | `u` (µm) | `z` (µm) | Edges |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ground `chip/GROUND_MINUS` (excluded) | 0 to 80 | 0 to 0.1 | `MA::chip/GROUND_MINUS__top::band=k` above, `MS::...__bottom::band=k` below, `MA::...__sidewall` at 80 |
| Gap (vacuum) | 80 to 86 | 0 to 0.1 | SA band edges at z = 0: band 0 from 80 to 80.5, band 1 to 81, band 2 to 85, then band 1 and band 0 up to the signal |
| Signal `chip/SIGNAL` (excluded) | 86 to 96 | 0 to 0.1 | MA top, MS bottom and MA sidewalls at 86 and 96 |
| Gap (vacuum) | 96 to 102 | 0 to 0.1 | SA bands as in the first gap |
| Ground `chip/GROUND_PLUS` (excluded) | 102 to 182 | 0 to 0.1 | as the first ground, sidewall at 102 |
| Substrate `D0_SUBSTRATE` | 0 to 182 | −500 to 0 | unbanded SA at its underside, `EXT` sidewalls at both ends |
| Vacuum `VACUUM_REGION` | 0 to 182 | −1500 to −500 and 0.1 to 1000.1 | `EXT` at the ends, top and bottom |

Here `u` is the distance along the cut and `z` the height. Each band of a gap
is measured from the nearer gap edge, so band 2 (beyond 1.0 µm) runs from 81 to
85 µm. In Route B a conductor is a rectangle of its film's thickness, excluded
from the domain and bounded by its MA top, MS bottom and MA sidewall edges. The
SA band edges are in the groups
`SA::D0_SUBSTRATE|VACUUM_REGION__interface::band=k`.

The cut is a `CutLine`, a straight segment along x or y in the plan's frame, in
micrometres:

```python
from scgsim.geometry.models.section import CutLine

cut = CutLine(start_um=(0.0, -91.0), end_um=(0.0, 91.0))
```

`scgsim.geometry.sgb.section.build_section_model(model, cut)` builds the
section from a validated 3D model and holds it in memory as a `SectionModel`.
Every part of it is the trace of a part of the 3D model:

| 2D model | Trace of | Group |
|---|---|---|
| Horizontal edge at height `z` | The horizontal face at that height, over the stretch of the cut it covers | That face's group, band index included |
| Vertical edge at `u` | The wall the cut crosses there | That wall's group (side walls carry no band) |
| Face | One connected part of a volume's cross-section; a volume the cut crosses twice gives two faces | The volume's, its owning Entity |
| End edges, top and bottom | The model's boundary walls and faces | `EXT::<domain>__<face kind>` |

The 3D model is always the whole layout, so every
[build rule](../supported-scope.qmd#layout-rules) applies to the whole layout,
also far from the cut.

### Cut rules {#cut-rules}

The 2D model stands for a line with one cross-section, so the cut must cross a
straight, uniform part of the line from one edge of the model to the other.
SGB refuses any other cut with an `InputError` that names what the cut meets,
the height, the place in micrometres and the fix.

| Rule | Refused cut | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Ends on the grid | An end off the model grid | Put both ends on the grid |
| Whole cross-section | An end beyond the model's planar extent (vacuum region included), an end inside the model where a region continues past it, or a stretch outside the model | Run the cut from one edge of the extent to the other |
| Right angle | A crossing at another angle: an oblique section widens the gaps and gives a plausible but wrong L and C | Cut where the line's edges run straight across the cut |
| No edge along the cut | The cut runs along an edge | Move the cut off the edge |
| No corner | The cut passes through a vertex of the layout or of a band seam | Move the cut along the line to a uniform section |
| No arc | The cut crosses an arc, or comes within half a grid step of one: a bend, a rounded corner, or a band seam turning round a corner | Move the cut onto a straight section, farther than the largest margin from a corner |
| No point contact | Conductors, or a conductor and the model's edge, touch only at a point in the section | Draw the conductors so that they overlap along an edge or stay apart, or move the cut |

## Preparation workers {#preparation-resources}

Preparation and meshing run serially. To give source preparation a pool of
workers, wrap the calls in `preparation_resources`:

```python
from scgsim.preparation import preparation_resources

with preparation_resources(max_workers=30):
    snapshot = plan.prepare()
    sim.set_plan(snapshot)
    sim.mesh()
```

`max_workers` bounds SCGSim's own preparation workers; on a cluster, request
the CPUs from the scheduler as well. Meshing runs on one Gmsh thread and
Palace's own MPI and OpenMP settings control the solve.
`scgsim.diagnostics.preparation_diagnostics(output_dir, profile=False)` records
stage timings.

## Input summary {#pre-solve-input-summary}

`sim.input_summary()` shows, before any file is written, what the model will
be: the source, Entities, occurrences, Nets, materials, heights, vacuum, ports,
EPR requests and solver settings, as a notebook card with the detached data in
`.data`. On Palace it shows the input `mesh()` will build, with the plan's
vacuum, its lumped elements and the route applied; `.data["backend"]["lumped_elements"]`
says what the simulation makes of each element. Unknown values stay
unknown, never zero. `scgsim.geometry.summarize_geometry_input(build_input,
*, prepared_stack)` gives the same summary of a normalized input.
